eli5.text: The internal tool that grades AI coding helpers now runs the Gemini 2.5 Flash model instead of Claude Sonnet when it calls an AI to review code. Anyone looking at the grading results will see feedback generated by the new model, and the tool is now marked as experimental so it can test cost-saving behavior. This only affects the automated evaluation system, not the AI you interact with directly.

ai.title: Fix ripgrep binary resolution in compiled Freebuff
ai.summary: New npm-app/src/native/ripgrep.ts resolves rg path dynamically, using @vscode/ripgrep in dev and self-extracting the embedded binary to ~/.config/manicode/rg in compiled mode. npm-app/src/tool-handlers.ts now awaits getRgPath() instead of static import, fixing ripgrep failures in Bun-compiled executables. npm-app/scripts/build-binary.js wraps string env defines in single quotes to prevent shell interpretation of spaces or special characters. Unix extraction runs chmod +x; failed extraction falls back to @vscode/ripgrep path.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant built as a standalone program (not running inside a code editor), the text-search feature now works again: the program unpacks its own search tool on first use and remembers where it put it, so searches stop failing. If you just updated to the latest version, the next time you trigger a code search you should see results come back instead of an error.

ai.title: README local setup instructions update
ai.summary: README local development steps simplified. Infisical CLI setup now includes `infisical secrets` verification instead of automatic injection note. Dependency installation consolidated to single `bun install` step, removing explicit `bun run build` requirement. Numbering corrected from 5 steps to 4.

eli5.text: People who help build this tool at their own computer will find simpler setup steps in the written instructions. The secret-code login process now asks you to double-check that your credentials are ready before starting, instead of relying on them loading themselves automatically, and the separate build step got folded into one installation command. If you tried to follow the old five-step guide, you'd hit missing steps and slightly out-of-order instructions; the written guide now matches what actually works.

ai.title: Version 1.0.338
ai.summary: Bump `codebuff` version to 1.0.338 in `npm-app/release/package.json`. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: The AI coding assistant you use got a small but useful refresh that fixes how it searches through your code on your own computer, so finding and working with your project files is more reliable. It also now runs a newer AI model when you ask it to evaluate changes using Git, which can make those code reviews more accurate, plus some background cleanup that keeps everything running smoothly without changing what you see. The changes are live today if you pull the latest version of the assistant.

ai.title: README Infisical steps renumbered
ai.summary: Infisical CLI setup steps in README.md changed from letters to numbers. Indentation adjusted for nested list alignment. Repo docs only.

eli5.text: The step-by-step instructions for connecting to the secure secrets storage tool now use numbered points (1, 2, 3, 4) instead of letters (a, b, c, d). This makes the list easier to follow and aligns the formatting with the surrounding numbered steps. Only the documentation was changed, so nothing about how the software runs was affected.

ai.title: Fix CheckpointManager listener leaks
ai.summary: Refactored `sendToWorker` in `npm-app/src/checkpoints/checkpoint-manager.ts` to use a shared `cleanup` function. This ensures `message` and `error` listeners are properly detached on success, error, or timeout, preventing accumulation. Also set `maxListeners` to 50 on the worker instance to suppress warnings during high-frequency operations.

eli5.text: The internal system that runs background tasks for the assistant was leaking small bits of memory every time it talked to a helper worker. Now those connections are cleaned up properly instead of piling up, so the system won't gradually slow down or hit resource limits during long sessions. This is live today and only affects how the assistant's own background processing stays healthy behind the scenes.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.339
ai.summary: Package version incremented from 1.0.338 to 1.0.339. Change applies to `npm-app/release/package.json`. No functional code or dependency updates included.

eli5.text: The software received a regular behind-the-scenes update to keep everything running smoothly and installs current. This update includes several smaller improvements: the setup guide now has clearer steps for connecting to a secrets tool, the system that tracks progress when working on code has been made more reliable, and the AI model used for evaluating changes has been switched to a newer version. These changes affect internal stability and guidance, but you wouldn't see dramatic new features from this update.

ai.title: Evals UI upgrade: avgTurns metric, model logos, display names
ai.summary: Evals table now computes avgTurns alongside avgScore and avgDuration, weighted by case count. getLogoForModel added to constants.ts resolves provider domains (google, anthropic, openai, deepseek) to Google favicon URLs for model rows. modelDisplayNames map in evals-table.tsx converts raw model IDs to friendly names like 'Gemini 2.5 Pro' and 'Claude 4 Opus'. Scope: common/src/constants.ts, web/src/app/evals/evals-table.tsx.

eli5.text: When you look at the evaluation results table, you'll now see a third average number called 'avgTurns' next to the score and duration columns, showing how many conversational rounds each test case took on average. Model names that previously appeared as cryptic strings like 'gemini-2.5-pro' or 'claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022' will display as friendlier names like 'Gemini 2.5 Pro' and 'Claude 4 Opus', and each model row will carry its provider's logo fetched from Google's favicon service. The averaging math was updated to weight all three metrics by how many test cases contributed each result, so larger benchmarks pull the averages more strongly. The friendly names and logo support are now in place and actively used by the table, so the new display is live today.

ai.title: Evals table UI tweaks and o3 Pro mapping
ai.summary: Evals table UI updated: model logos enlarged from 16px to 256px (sz=256 in getLogoForModel) and rendered at w-6 h-6 with wider spacing (space-x-3). Benchmark progress bars resized to w-36 h-8. Added 'o3-pro-2025-06-10' to modelDisplayNames map in web/src/app/evals/evals-table.tsx.

eli5.text: The evaluation results table now shows larger model logos and wider spacing between columns, making each model's name and icon easier to read at a glance. Progress bars that track benchmark completion have also been resized for better visibility. The table now recognizes and displays the name for a newly added model called o3-pro-2025-06-10, so it appears with a friendly label instead of its raw identifier. These are visual refinements to an admin-facing evals dashboard, live today.

ai.title: Add CODEBUFF tool format instruction to backend/src/tools.ts
ai.summary: Added a developer comment in `backend/src/tools.ts` instructing CODEBUFF to use system-provided tool formats instead of file-local definitions. This clarifies internal tooling conventions without altering runtime behavior. Scope limited to source code comments. No functional changes to tool execution or API surfaces.

eli5.text: A single line was added to the top of an internal instructions file that developers use to guide an AI coding assistant. The line is a note telling the assistant to follow the official tool-format guidance that comes from the system rather than copying whatever tool-format example happens to exist in that same file. You would only notice anything if you opened that instructions file and looked at the very first comment, because the note is only a comment, it does not change how anything actually runs.

ai.title: Generalize syncfailure table schema and logging
ai.summary: Renamed `message_id` column to `id` in `sync_failure` table and removed default provider constraint. Updated `logSyncFailure` utility to accept provider argument, decoupling failure tracking from specific message contexts. Affects backend `message-cost-tracker.ts`, common `sync-failure.ts`, and database schema migrations.

eli5.text: The system that tracks when billing data fails to reach Stripe from your assistants just got more flexible. Previously, every recorded failure had to be tied to a specific assistant message, and Stripe was the only provider it could handle. Now, failures can be filed by provider name without needing a message link, so it can track billing sync problems across different providers, not just Stripe. This is an internal cleanup, so you won't see a visible change unless a billing sync fails, in which case the error log will now show the provider that caused it.

ai.title: Fix credit granting idempotency
ai.summary: Refactors duplicate handling in packages/billing/src/grant-credits.ts. Replaces strict error code and constraint checks with helper matching code 23505 or message containing already exists. Ensures concurrent requests skip grants safely without throwing.

eli5.text: When the system tries to give you store credit and two requests arrive at the same instant, it used to crash and report a duplicate error to you. Now it simply recognizes that the credit was already handed out and quietly moves on, so you no longer see an error message during those split-second overlaps. The change is behind the scenes and already live, affecting only those moments when simultaneous credit grants collide.
